scores.question: Did Nvidia deliver on what it said in May 2024 about Blackwell chips reaching the market later that year?
failure_details: 0 llm_unsupported: Opening: Nvidia did not deliver on timing given in May 2024, verdicts differ by claim.: Tool verdicts are mixed (walked_back, delivered_late); the 'Mostly no' summary is a conclusion the cited items o
1 llm_unsupported: An April 2024 10-Q said Blackwell customer shipments would ramp in the second half of the fiscal year.: No citation; no April 2024 10-Q item is in the evidence.

2 llm_unsupported: Tool rates market claim walked_back: no shipments by Dec 31, 2024: E17 reasoning says no item clearly shows shipments by 2024-12-31; it does not state the 'no shipments' finding as fact, though close.

2 llm_unsupported: 2024 filings described ramp as planned for fiscal Q4 2025; later filings reported Blackwell revenue in FY2026: Cited E13 is a news item only; it does not state the filing details, which are in outcome
scores.answer:
Nvidia's May 2024 Blackwell timing claims received four scored verdicts from the tool: three "walked_back" and one "delivered_late." - **Shipping start in Q2 2024:** Huang said Blackwell chips would start shipping in the second quarter, with production ramping in the third quarter, as reported by Business Insider [1]. The tool rates this "walked_back" because later filings moved shipments to Q4 (reported by businessinsider.com) [1]. Nvidia's July 2024 10-Q said the Blackwell production ramp was scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter [2]. - **Arriving on the market later in 2024:** CNBC reported that Blackwell-based chips were expected to begin hitting the market later that year (reported by cnbc.com) [3]. The tool rates this "walked_back" because no item shows shipments beginning by December 31, 2024 (reported by cnbc.com) [3]. Nvidia's 10-Q for the quarter ended April 2024 had said it expected to ramp Blackwell customer shipments in the second half of the fiscal year [4]. - **Data centers running on Blackwell by Q4:** Business Insider reported this claim (reported by businessinsider.com) [1]. The tool rates it "walked_back" because the FY2025 filings described Blackwell production and shipments as scheduled for Q4, and later filings show the ramp moved later (reported by businessinsider.com) [1]. - **Launch by end of 2024:** Fortune reported that Nvidia said it would get a later-year revenue boost from the Blackwell launch (reported by fortune.com) [5]. The tool rates this "delivered_late," 239 days late (reported by fortune.com) [5]. That reasoning is thin, so this is the weakest of the four verdicts. Huang's May 2024 statement that Blackwell was "in full production" was not scored because it had no checkable target (reported by finance.yahoo.com) [6].
Left out because they could not be verified (not supported by the cited evidence): one statement.

scores.question: Did Nvidia keep its promise to pay the raised dividend on June 28, 2024?
failure_details: 0 llm_prefer_primary: Payment was to be $0.10 per share to holders of record on June 11: E11 is news only; the 10-Q gives $0.01 post-split for the same record date and payment, so the filing should be cited.

0 llm_unsupported: The only quarter in that window still paid $0.04: E9 says the dividend was $0.04 in FY2025Q1 but the cited item only says the increase was announced; it does not state the paid rate of $0.04.

1 llm_unsupported: $0.01 post-split equals the $0.10 pre-split rate announced in May 2024: Cited items give $0.10 pre-split rate in May but never state the $0.01 post-split equivalence; the 10-for-1 split is only implie

2 llm_unsupported: The tool scores that promise as delivered, based on the filing.: Cited E3 is the news item; its verdict 'delivered' rests on E2 which is cited only in the first sentence, but E3 itself cites E2 as out
scores.answer:
Yes. Nvidia's 10-Q says it "increased our quarterly cash dividend to $0.01 per share on a post-Stock Split basis to all shareholders of record on June 11, 2024," and that "our quarterly cash dividend was paid on June 28, 2024" [1]. The promise, as reported by fool.com, was that the first increased dividend would be paid on June 28 [2]. The 10-Q's figure is post-split. The split itself was a ten-for-one split effective June 7, 2024 [3]. A separate promise, that the quarterly dividend would reach at least $0.10 in a quarter ending by June 28, 2024, was rated "cannot_determine" by the tool, because no item in that window shows the $0.10 rate being paid (reported by fool.com) [4].
Left out because they could not be verified (not supported by the cited evidence): one statement.

scores.answer:
AMD's $2 billion AI-revenue forecast for 2024 cannot be scored as delivered or missed (reported by fool.com) [1]. The only record I found is a Motley Fool article from January 13, 2024, reporting the forecast, and the tool does not name the speaker (reported by fool.com) [1]. Its verdict is "not comparable" because the target is a segment figure while reported values are company totals (reported by fool.com) [1]. Data Center revenue for 2024 was $12.6 billion, up 94% from 2023, driven by Instinct GPU and EPYC CPU sales [2].

scores.question: Did Jensen Huang deliver on his promise that Nvidia is poised for its next wave of growth?
failure_details: 0 llm_unsupported: No stored promise matches 'poised for its next wave of growth'.: No cited evidence addresses the promise tracker or a search result; no citation given.
0 llm_unsupported: The promise tracker returned no Jensen Huang claims for Nvidia.: No cited evidence describes the tracker's results.
scores.answer:
Huang did say it, but the claim cannot be scored, so there is no verdict on whether he delivered.
On May 22, 2024, he said "We are poised for our next wave of growth," as reported by Fortune [1], Yahoo Finance [2] and Business Insider, which quoted it from the earnings call [3]. The claim is vague: it has no checkable target or deadline, so it is not scored and I cannot say whether he delivered on it (reported by fortune.com) [1].
Separately, news reports from fool.com say Huang is confident Nvidia's growth will continue unabated next year [4] and that the number of chips Nvidia sells will double in 2027 (reported by fool.com) [4]. Neither is scored, because the metric is not tracked in Nvidia's reported financials.
